transcript: Dead As A Dodo is my favorite new theater piece of the year so far. This is a delightfully inventive musical odyssey about two friends, a boy and a dodo bird, who are both skeletons. The plot is somewhat of a hero's journey, but it really serves as the structure to showcase a bunch of different settings and characters. The entire story is told through puppetry and voice acting, blending theatricality with a gorgeous cinematic quality. The level of precision in the movement of the ensemble is a huge part of what makes the magic happen, along with the genius puppetry, lighting, and projection designs. It’s truly a melting pot of memorable visual surprises, but I also found the light hearted and humorous story surprisingly poignant. I would highly recommend checking this out as it's only running through February 9th at Baruch's Performing Arts Center. With that, another program for my collection.
